findings.premise: The `.insrc-artifact` / `.insrc-diagram` class names the design introduces as a brand-new harmonizing DOM convention do not already carry a different meaning elsewhere in the codebase.
findings.evidence: `.insrc-artifact` (and `.insrc-artifact-*` subclasses) is already a live, styled CSS class used by the daemon's separate chat-embedded artifact-preview templates (src/assets/artifacts/templates/er.html etc., loaded via src/daemon/artifacts/template-loader.ts), with its own VS Code-themed styling (`.insrc-artifact-er { ... background: var(--vscode-editor-background, #12151e) ... }`) and its own `.insrc-artifact pre.mermaid` Mermaid selector (src/assets/artifacts/templates/_renderer.html:28). The LLD's citations ([[c1]]–[[c5]]) and data-model section never acknowledge this prior claim on the exact class name, so the design's framing of `.insrc-artifact` as a fresh, single-meaning selector for 'the shared override CSS' is not accurate — the name is already overloaded in the codebase (a different, unrelated artifact-kind template system). This is not a runtime collision today (the two never share a DOM — the chat-embed templates and the companion/docgen standalone HTML files are rendered in entirely separate documents), so it does not break anything as written, but it undermines the design's own stated goal (R1: 'Central visual policy... single source') of `.insrc-artifact` meaning one coherent thing, and risks future confusion if the chat-embed preview and a companion/docgen export are ever composed on the same page. [files: src/assets/artifacts/templates/er.html, src/assets/artifacts/templates/_renderer.html, src/daemon/artifacts/template-loader.ts]
findings.action: Author should note the existing `.insrc-artifact*` usage in src/assets/artifacts/templates/ in the LLD's references/alternatives, and either pick a differently-scoped class (e.g. a two-token wrapper unique to this feature) or explicitly document why reusing the name for a disjoint document type is safe.

findings.evidence: Both renderCompanionPage and assembleShell are pure functions returning a single HTML string with no database or graph write (confirmed by reading both files end-to-end — no db/graph import in either). An old generated HTML file has no `insrc-theme` meta tag today (that tag doesn't exist in current output) and is not re-opened or rewritten by any code path found in these modules, so adding a new meta tag to newly-generated files cannot retroactively affect already-written files on disk, matching the 'zero downtime / no data rewrite' claim.
